title: 📓 Syntopy in North American Passerines
text:
📓 Syntopy in North American Passerines
Here is the documentation of my master’s thesis in ecology.






Here I focus on building a conceptual tool for my thesis, where I analyse local co-occurrence (syntopy) on two spatial scales (between and withing transects) using data from Breeding Bird Survey.



View Thesis Documentation →



🌎 SDS Assignment
Here you can check my final assignement of Spatial Data Science for Social Geography course, which is a computational essey written in 🐍python using JupyterLab.






I made the route-based analysis of species richness across the contiguous United States, using The North American Breeding Bird Survey (BBS) data - routes as the observational units and combination of environmental (NDVI) and spatial (elevation, LONG, LAT) predictors.

title: Matěj Tvarůžka
text:
I have been fascinated by nature for as long as I can remember, with David Attenborough’s documentaries serving as my earliest and most inspiring source of curiosity about the natural world. I began birdwatching in 2018 — a hobby that has since evolved into my main academic focus, as birds have become my primary study group. This passion led me to pursue studies in ecological and evolutionary biology, which remain at the core of my scientific interests.
I am currently a Master’s student of Ecology at Charles University in Prague, working under the supervision of Prof. Vladimír Remeš. I draw inspiration from scientists such as E. O. Wilson, Jared Diamond, Richard Feynman, and Vojtěch Novotný, whose work continues to shape my perspective on the diversity and complexity of life. Beyond research, I enjoy exploring topics in politics, history, and sociology. I am also passionate about jazz music — I play drums and percussion, dance swing, and can sometimes be found at my favorite Prague jazz club, U Malého Glena.
